title: GJ 3378 b: A Nearby Habitable-Zone Super-Earth Around a Red Dwarf
abstract: GJ 3378 b is a 2.3 Earth-mass planet orbiting a red dwarf at 25 light-years. It receives 90% of Earth's solar flux, placing it in the conservative habitable zone. However, red dwarf flares may strip atmospheres, and tidal locking creates extreme day/night temperature gradients. The star's longevity (hundreds of billions of years) makes it a compelling long-term target for human migration.

c9_implications.habitability: Tidal locking + flare activity are major uncertainties. Atmospheric retention models needed.
c9_implications.longevity: Red dwarf lifespan >> Sun's remaining habitable window (~1 Gyr). Strategic target for cosmic continuity.
c9_implications.assembly_index: Planetary system A_c would include orbital resonance stability, atmospheric chemistry complexity, and stellar activity coupling.
